- Breast density assessment — relevant for mammographic sensitivity and differential weight of imaging features  
- Mass size or growth trajectory quantification (e.g., serial measurements) — would strengthen concern for aggressiveness  

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Invasive ductal carcinoma

gaps.info: Core needle biopsy histopathology (e.g., presence of stromal invasion, epithelial atypia, mitotic rate) and IHC markers (ER/PR/HER2 status)

gaps.info: Clinical axillary lymph node exam findings (not just patient self-report)
gaps.discriminates: Early-stage invasive carcinoma (clinically node-negative) vs. locally advanced disease (node-positive), and informs staging urgency

The patient is a 48-year-old premenopausal woman with a rapidly enlarging, asymptomatic left breast mass discovered over 4 weeks — a timeframe highly suggestive of aggressive biology.
